answer: Memory-hard proofs price each identity in exclusive RAM. A crystal, a 256-bit window seed, opens 60 seconds for each key to finish an ivory bound to its address and that seed while holding 2 GB of memory. A host cannot complete a second ivory on the same 2 GB before the window ends; a reused or missing proof is written as a fable and burns 25 POA. A farm of 500 keys sharing one 2 GB host finishes one ivory; each of the other 499 receives a fable: 499 x 25 POA = 12,475 POA the attacker forfeits.
